final_report.topic: Speculative Decoding and Medusa Multi-Head Architectures for LLM Inference
final_report.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference: A Comparative Analysis of Speculative Decoding and Medusa Multi-Head Architectures

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Speculative decoding and Medusa multi-head architectures offer prominent pathways for accelerating large language model inference. Speculative decoding leverages a smaller draft model alongside a target model [cite_exec_1], whereas Medusa eliminates the separate draft model by integrating lightweight feedforward heads directly onto a frozen base transformer [cite_exec_2].

claims.text: Speculative decoding pairs a small draft model with a large target model to accelerate inference.

sections.title: Architectural Mechanisms and Performance
sections.content: Speculative decoding generates gamma candidate tokens in parallel and validates them in a single target forward pass using modified rejection sampling [cite_mech_1]. When the draft acceptance rate exceeds 75%, it achieves a 2.3x to 2.8x wall-clock speedup on 70B parameter models without altering the output probability distribution [cite_mech_2]. Conversely, Medusa utilizes tree-structured attention masks to validate candidate token paths concurrently, delivering a 2.2x speedup on single-GPU deployments [cite_mech_3]. Furthermore, Medusa avoids the additional 4GB VRAM footprint typically required to host a separate 7B draft model [cite_mech_4].

conclusion.title: Conclusion and Implications
conclusion.content: Both speculative decoding and Medusa provide robust acceleration for large language models, balancing compute efficiency and memory footprints differently [cite_conc_2]. While standard speculative decoding provides high speedups on massive parameter scales given high acceptance rates [cite_conc_1], Medusa offers a memory-efficient single-GPU alternative through integrated multi-head prediction [cite_conc_3].

claims.text: Speculative decoding provides substantial speedups at high parameter scales given favorable acceptance rates, whereas Medusa provides a memory-efficient single-GPU alternative.

Specific draft acceptance rate thresholds for Medusa architectures were not detailed in the available context.
